      <title>‘Elonville’: US residents say Musk’s xAI offered to buy homes if they don’t sue over datacenter noise</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/28/datacenter-noise-lawsuit-elon-musk-mississippi</link>
      <description><p>Several Mississippi homes have been purchased near datacenters and one resident said realtor outlined target to buy more than 400</p><p>People in a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/mississippi">Mississippi</a> neighborhood, many of whom dislike a nearby power plant central to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/elon-musk">Elon Musk</a>’s artificial intelligence ambitions, have received a stark offer – to sell their houses to his company and make way.</p><p>Real estate agents have been going door to door in Southaven, Mississippi, on behalf of xAI, touting a deal to purchase houses as long as the owners agree to not join a lawsuit against the company over the power plant’s noise. (Musk’s AI company officially became SpaceXAI in July and has lately been rebranded as SpaceXSI but to neighbors of the datacenter in Mississippi, it remains xAI.)</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/28/datacenter-noise-lawsuit-elon-musk-mississippi">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Castle Walls review – Prime’s first fully AI-generated show is here, and it’s a Vaseline-smeared mess</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2026/oct/29/castle-walls-review-prime-first-fully-ai-generated-tv-show</link>
      <description><p>Billed as the first end-to-end AI-created series on a major streaming service, this Turkish show looks like the result of the prompt ‘make it cinematic’</p><p>Just as the world reels from Elon Musk’s AI-powered <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/oct/27/elon-musk-ai-odyssey-movie-grok-christopher-nolan">The Odyssey remake</a> – though “remake” feels rather generous for a seven-minute splat of synthetic sludge – another bucket of AI gunk is dropped on to our faces. For Prime Video’s AI-generated TV series Castle Walls, produced by Turkish production studio Ay Yapım using a melange of generative video tools, has arrived, billed as the first end-to-end AI-created series to premiere on a major streaming platform.</p><p>It’s certainly more epic than Musk’s production, consisting of two 17-minute episodes. Set in the 11th century, the show revolves around the historic Alamut Castle, although it’s entirely absent of any real sense of time or place. I was briefly intrigued by the opening images, with their bold palette of blues and mustard browns and yellows – but as soon as the “people” appeared, looking like Vaseline-smeared Madame Tussauds creations slowly melting in the sun, everything came crashing down.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2026/oct/29/castle-walls-review-prime-first-fully-ai-generated-tv-show">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Meta plans $95bn stock offering to help cover AI expansion</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/oct/26/meta-plans-95bn-stock-offering-to-help-cover-ai-expansion</link>
      <description><p>Tech firm announces two-part fundraising after Elon Musk warns hundreds of AI startups face collapse</p><p>Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta has announced plans for $95bn (£71bn) of fundraising to cover its AI expenditure, even as Elon Musk warned that funding for smaller players in the sector was drying up.</p><p>The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp is a leading investor in AI and is ploughing multibillion-dollar sums into datacentres, the central nervous systems of the technology.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/oct/26/meta-plans-95bn-stock-offering-to-help-cover-ai-expansion">Continue reading...</a></description>
